title: src/main.mockruns.test.ts:197 session created with fixedClock but main uses systemClock

question: Q-003
reason: Verified in the files: the test at src/main.mockruns.test.ts:197 uses fixedClock(NOW) with NOW 2026-11-02T10:00:00Z and passes it to seedFlowActors, createTestSession and seedMockRunFlows; createSession writes last_seen_at from that clock with IDLE_TIMEOUT_S 1800; resolveSession marks the session expired when now >= last_seen_at + idle timeout; src/api/session-auth.ts resolves with deps.clock, which main sets to systemClock; MainDeps has no clock member; src/main.runs.test.ts uses systemClock for the same setup. The suggestion names the frozen test file and is the only fix that does not change production design.

checked.claim: The second wiring test creates its session, actors and seed with a fixed clock.
The fixed clock is set to 2 November 2026, days before the real clock.

checked.quote: const alice: Session = await createTestSession(db, a, "alice", clock);
checked.claim: Alice's session is created with the fixed clock.

checked.quote: const { sessionId } = await createSession(tx, ctx, { userId: user.userId }, { clock });
checked.claim: The test session helper passes the given clock to createSession.
Sessions expire after 1800 seconds of idleness.
resolveSession treats a session as expired when the resolving clock's now is past last_seen_at plus the idle timeout.
The PEP resolves the cookie with its own deps.clock.
main builds the PEP with systemClock.
MainDeps has no clock member, so a test cannot inject a clock into main.
The existing runs wiring test uses systemClock for its session setup, the pattern the suggestion follows.
